summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and history of gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcers (medically treated with resolution) was admitted for persistent nausea/vomiting with poor oral intake and protein-calorie malnutrition while dependent on TPN via a tunneled right internal jugular catheter. She underwent uncomplicated laparoscopic gastrostomy tube placement on 2170-01-16. A postoperative gastrografin study confirmed correct tube position, after which tube feeds (Fibersource HN) were initiated and advanced without worsening baseline nausea; TPN was discontinued on postoperative day 1. By hospital day 3 she reached goal nocturnal cycled tube feeds (80 mL/hr for 12 hours), tolerated a stage V diet in small amounts, and home services were arranged for tube feeding support. With stable enteral nutrition, Interventional Radiology removed the tunneled catheter without complication, and she was discharged home ambulatory and stable with tube care instructions, residual checks, return precautions, and continuation of an oral proton pump inhibitor with surgical follow-up.
